caseText: A one-year-old boy with macrocephaly, excessive growth, characteristic facial features and developmental delay had a pathogenic NSD1 variant and was diagnosed with Sotos syndrome. Intervention: The report describes three months of combined traditional Chinese medicine and rehabilitation. Outcome: The authors reported improvement in global development after the combined treatment, while also noting that the condition has no radical cure.
target: Train the model to separate confirmed biomedical diagnosis from supportive TCM/rehabilitation management and to avoid turning a single case report into a general efficacy claim.

caseText: A 32-year-old man had severe plaque psoriasis with recurrent erythematous scaling for about one year together with metabolic abnormalities and psychiatric symptoms. Intervention: The reported intervention was oral Chinese herbal medicine. Outcome: The report described improvement in skin findings and several metabolic-related indices after treatment.
target: Use as a case-reasoning example that preserves the single-patient evidence level and distinguishes observed outcome from proof of general treatment efficacy.

caseText: A 56-year-old woman with long-standing dry eye and dry mouth was diagnosed with primary Sjögren syndrome after clinical testing and labial gland biopsy. The report described a mixed cold-heat and cold-dampness TCM pattern. Intervention: Modified Da-Chai-Hu decoction and Linggui Zhugan decoction were used after prior therapies did not adequately control symptoms. Outcome: The patient reported improvement in dryness-related symptoms and sleep quality after eight weeks.
target: Teach layered reasoning: biomedical diagnosis is established by clinical testing, while TCM pattern differentiation is a separate interpretive layer used to guide the reported herbal approach.

caseText: A 65-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis had progressive diabetic foot gangrene, severe atherosclerosis and elevated inflammatory markers despite prior conventional management. Intervention: The published case used an integrated outpatient protocol combining a Chinese herbal decoction with debridement and local analgesia over seven months. Outcome: The report described complete ulcer healing, reduced inflammatory markers and preservation of foot function.
target: Train the model to recognize multimodal care, comorbidity burden, objective follow-up markers and the limits of causal inference from one case.

caseText: A 53-year-old woman had a long history of recurrent refractory Crohn disease with chronic indigestion, reflux, abdominal pain and diarrhea despite pharmacologic and surgical treatment. Intervention: The report describes weekly acupuncture for 21 sessions plus Chinese herbal medicine as needed, alongside ongoing pharmacologic therapy. Outcome: The patient reported improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms and reduced medication dosage.
target: Use to train cautious multimodal reasoning: preserve the established Crohn diagnosis, identify adjunctive TCM use, and avoid extrapolating a single subjective response to population-level efficacy.

caseText: A 73-year-old woman developed a persistent black tongue with thirst and diarrhea after hospitalization and antibiotic exposure. The report documented a thick black coating surrounded by thick white coating, a medium-sized tongue with tooth marks, and a light-red tongue body. Intervention: Using the four TCM diagnostic methods, the authors described a pattern of spleen Qi deficiency with turbid dampness and used a modified herbal formula based on Wu-Ling-San and Da-Yuan-Yin. Outcome: The report described near resolution after two weeks and complete resolution after four weeks.
target: High-priority tongue case for teaching structured observation -> TCM pattern interpretation -> intervention -> follow-up, while retaining the distinction between an observed case and a validated diagnostic rule.
